newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SDP MPS SEEN DEBATING GOVT SEATS THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SDP MPS SEEN DEBATING GOVT SEATS THURSDAY.

text.p: Social Democratic Party (SDP) MPs are likely to debate possible changes to the party's group of ministers in their weekly meeting on Thursday but no decisions will be made, SDP sources said on Wednesday. The party's losses in European and local elections on October 20 increased pressure to find scapegoats and change ministers and most eyes are turned to second Finance Minister Arja Alho who has long had thin support among MPs, they said.
"I would be surprised if the issue did not come up," said SDP's parliamentary group secretary Sisko Seppa.

Finnish media has reported that Alho's chances of staying in government were reduced by oppotion allegations last week that she had given secret information to the counterparty ahead of talks to link the markka to the ERM on October 12.
Arja Alho said on television on Tuesday that on the day before the ERM link she had contacted EU commissioner h Finance Minister Ruari Quinn.
Asked if Finland's negotiation targets were in a particular range, she said, "yes it is".
The opposition Centre Party last week notified the Chancellor of Justice about this. On Monday he started an inquiry.

The SDP parliamentary group will not decide about Alho's future until the chancellor has ended his preliminary investigation, but even if he were to clear Alho of all suspicion she may still have to go, the sources said.
"The pressures would ease but not go away," one SDP source said.
Media commentators have even said Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen is now Alho's only supporter.

He has repeatedly defended her actions, saying she acted in line with instructions and totally in the country's interest. Lipponen has also said EU representatives have described Finland's ERM-peg as "a perfect operation".

But according to Finland's Money Act, information about the markka's exchange rate when it is linked to any currency system can not be given out by the government or the Bank of Finland until the government has made a final decision.
However, Alho on Tuesday said a pegging operation could not even have been started without stating some indication about the levels of a link.

Another factor in the debate is the fact that on the Saturday evening when the link was announnish television broadcast the likely level of the markka's central parity rate against the Ecu well before it was announced.
According to Lipponen this information was leaked in Finland, though it had nothing to do with Arja Alho's case.
